prerequisites: Achieved the second study section (at least 42 ECTS points from the first study section)
Previous attendance of a module with content on operating systems

learning_outcomes.text: Know and evaluate specific characteristics and requirements for embedded systems.
Know, compare, and evaluate hardware for embedded systems.

Know scheduling procedures for embedded real-time systems (Fixed-Priority, Earliest Deadline First, Time-Triggered, PFair) on single and multicore architectures for independent and dependent tasks, implement them as part of embedded software, and verify content.
Know and apply problems and solutions for accessing resources in embedded systems.
Know and evaluate real-time operating systems such as VxWorks, Embedded Linux, OSEK-OS/AUTOSAR-OS.
Design, implement, and verify software as part of a system solution, considering specific requirements for embedded systems in airplanes and vehicles.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Definitions and examples, characteristics of embedded systems and cyber-physical systems (CPS)
Hardware of embedded systems: Overview, sensors and actuators, processors, memory, input/output and communication
Scheduling: Basic concepts, scheduling algorithms for real-time systems (EDF, RMS, DMS, TS), dependent tasks, resource access
Real-time operating systems: Overview, OSEK-OS, AUTOSAR-OS, VxWorks, Embedded Linux
Programming embedded systems: Imperative languages, object-orientation
assessment_rules: The assessment is based on a 90-minute written examination. Bonus points, up to a maximum of 5% of the points awarded in the exam, can be given for practical work. The exact conditions for bonus points are detailed in the Moodle course room.
